title: Sansara

teacherSummary.text: Over many years Siddhartha grows wealthy, gambles, drinks, and becomes greedy and weary—like the childlike people. Kamala tells him she wishes to learn about Gotama. After a dream of Kamala's songbird lying dead in its golden cage, Siddhartha feels disgust at his life and leaves the city without a word. Kamala, pregnant with his child, frees her bird.

framing.script: Teacher reads aloud before the reading. Before we read the next chapters, I want to tell you about part of this story. After years of wealth and pleasure, Siddhartha feels empty and disgusted with his life. He leaves the city, and at a river he thinks about ending his life. He doesn't. The sacred word Om comes to him, he sleeps, and he wakes up feeling renewed. Hesse calls the wish an error that Siddhartha wakes up from, and the rest of the book is about finding peace and love. No one in the novel dies by suicide. So let's be clear: hurting yourself is wrong and is never the answer.
